elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once per 12 months.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that audits may occur “no more than once per 12 months.”

elements.element: Customer must receive at least 30 days’ prior notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: The clause requires “not less than 30 days’ prior” notice.

elements.element: The audit notice must be written.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires “prior written notice.”

elements.element: Audits must be conducted during business hours.
elements.evidence: The added operative sentence expressly limits audits to business hours.

The phrase “an independent Certified Public Accountant or other Audit Professional” does not unambiguously require the alternative “other Audit Professional” to be independent. Mutual selection does not cure that omission.

elements.element: The auditor must be bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires an auditor “bound by confidentiality obligations.”

elements.element: Vendor bears the audit cost by default.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Licensor, corresponding to Vendor, bears the audit cost unless the stated exception applies.

elements.element: Audit costs may be shifted to Customer only if an underpayment exceeds 5%.
elements.evidence: The clause shifts costs upon any “discrepancy” exceeding 5%, rather than specifically an underpayment exceeding 5%. A discrepancy could include another type of variance.

elements.element: The audit must not include direct access to Customer’s systems.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that no audit may include direct access to Licensee’s systems.

elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The stricter rolling cap of no more than once per 12 months satisfies an annual frequency cap.

elements.element: Customer must receive at least 15 days’ prior notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: The clause requires at least 30 days’ prior written notice, which exceeds the fallback notice period.

elements.element: Vendor bears the audit cost by default.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Licensor, corresponding to Vendor, bears the audit cost unless the exception applies.

elements.element: Audit costs may be shifted to Customer only if an underpayment exceeds 10%.
elements.evidence: The clause permits cost shifting for a discrepancy exceeding 5%, including discrepancies between 5% and 10%, and does not limit the trigger to an underpayment.

result.reason: Neither level is fully satisfied. The preferred position lacks an unambiguous independence requirement for every permitted auditor and uses a general 5% “discrepancy” trigger rather than a 5% underpayment trigger. The fallback fails because it permits cost shifting above 5% instead of only for underpayments exceeding 10%. The redline is also non-minimal because it adds an off-site-audit requirement not contained in either position. The existing scope and mutual-selection terms remain operative, although the combination of an audit within 30 days and at least 30 days’ notice effectively compresses scheduling to approximately day 30.
